River cleanup draws hundreds

More than three hundred volunteers turned out on Saturday morning for the annual Clear River cleanup, hauling tires, shopping carts and an old canoe out of the water near the Elm Street bridge.

Organizers said this year's turnout was the largest since the event began fourteen years ago. Local businesses donated gloves, bags and lunch for everyone who took part, and the high school band played from the riverbank.

The city's parks department will haul away the collected debris on Monday. Volunteers who want to help with next spring's planting day can sign up at the library.
